note: French says 'you did not learn to speak French'; English changes this to present inability/knowledge.
proposed_target: Je sais que tu n'as pas appris à parler français.
proposed_english: I know you didn't learn to speak French.

note: J'ai dû laisser expresses a strong inference ('must have left'), not weak possibility 'may have left'.
proposed_target: J'ai dû laisser mon portefeuille dans le bus.
proposed_english: I must have left my wallet on the bus.

note: sur le chemin de l'école à la maison is awkward/nonstandard for 'on my way home from school'; use natural French.
proposed_target: Je l'ai rencontré en rentrant de l'école.
proposed_english: I met him on my way home from school.

note: passer means come/stop by; English adds the purpose 'to see me'.
proposed_target: Même si elle devait passer, dis-lui que je ne suis pas à la maison.
proposed_english: Even if she stops by, tell her I am not at home.

note: Natural English requires 'ask for help', not 'ask help from'.
proposed_target: C'est la dernière personne à qui je demanderais de l'aide, car il n'est pas du tout fiable.
proposed_english: He's the last person I would ask for help, because he is completely unreliable.

note: French asks whether the speaker speaks French well enough; English adds can/ability.
proposed_target: Je ne sais pas si je parle assez bien français pour pouvoir expliquer ceci correctement.
proposed_english: I don't know if I speak French well enough to explain this properly.

note: After negative Je ne pense pas que, standard French requires the subjunctive j'aie.
proposed_target: Je ne pense pas que j'aie envie de répondre à plus de tes questions pour l'instant.
proposed_english: I don't think I want to answer any more of your questions right now.

note: Je ne voudrais pas is conditional/polite 'I wouldn't want', not simple present 'I don't want'.
proposed_target: Je ne voudrais pas te presser, mais essayons de prendre le prochain bus.
proposed_english: I wouldn't want to rush you, but let's try to catch the next bus.

note: French means the speaker cannot understand what drives some people to troll forums; English invents a 'what goes through their minds' formulation.
proposed_target: Je n'arrive pas à comprendre les raisons qui poussent certaines personnes à parasiter les forums.
proposed_english: I can't understand what drives some people to troll forums.

note: serrer dans ses bras means hug; English 'hold me' is less exact.
proposed_target: J'ai besoin que quelqu'un me serre dans ses bras et me dise que tout ira bien.
proposed_english: I need someone to hug me and tell me everything will be all right.

note: English 'used to never eat' is awkward; preserve the habitual past naturally.
proposed_target: Je me rappelle quand nous ne mangions jamais de légumes que nous n'avions pas cultivés nous-mêmes.
proposed_english: I remember when we never ate vegetables that we hadn't grown ourselves.

note: gérer les déchets means manage/handle waste; English 'disposing of waste' narrows the meaning.
proposed_target: Je pense qu'il est temps de changer nos façons de gérer les déchets.
proposed_english: I think it is about time we changed our ways of managing waste.

note: For polished standard French, prefer ce serait over colloquial ça serait in this workbook register.
proposed_target: Je pense que ce serait une bonne idée pour toi d'étudier le français.
proposed_english: I think that it would be a good idea for you to study French.

note: en fait means actually/in fact; English 'as it is' is not the direct equivalent.
proposed_target: Je pensais que les choses allaient s'améliorer mais en fait elles ne font qu'empirer.
proposed_english: I thought things would get better, but in fact they are only getting worse.

note: présentement is regionally marked; use maintenant for broadly standard learner French.
proposed_target: Je veux passer un coup de téléphone, mais je n'ai pas de monnaie maintenant.
proposed_english: I want to make a phone call, but I don't have any change now.
